title: Act I, Scene I
focus: the tribunes and the fickle crowd

teacherSummary.text: Commoners take a holiday to celebrate Caesar's triumph over Pompey's sons. The tribunes Flavius and Marullus scold them; a cobbler answers with puns. Marullus reminds them they once cheered Pompey, calls them ungrateful, and sends them home. The tribunes then go to strip decorations from Caesar's statues so that he will not soar 'above the view of men.'

context.history: Tribunes were officials elected to protect ordinary citizens (plebeians). Caesar had defeated Pompey in civil war and then Pompey's sons in 45 BC. Celebrating a victory over fellow Romans was controversial.

significance: The first scene introduces the crowd as changeable: it cheered Pompey and now cheers Caesar. That sets up Act III, when Brutus and then Antony each win the same crowd within minutes.
